title: Which Elevation Certificate Sets the Elevation Multiplier on an Excess Flood Renewal
content:
The elevation multiplier of an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** renewal term premium is read from one Elevation Certificate, chosen as follows.

## Rule

Where the policy record carries an accepted Elevation Certificate, the elevation multiplier is read from that certificate's whole-foot figure; where the policy record carries none but the NFIP policy of the home holds an applied certificate, the one received latest, surveyed no more than the tier's maximum certificate age, counted in whole months (twelve for each year), before the date it was received, the elevation multiplier is read from that certificate instead, comparing the lowest floor elevation it certifies less the base flood elevation it certifies with the tier's credit threshold; where neither record carries such a certificate, the elevation multiplier is one.

The NFIP policy of the home is the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)) in force whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record, and the HomeFlood policy of the home is the active Tidemark HomeFlood policy whose policy number is that underlying policy number; of these two policies only their status, the NFIP policy's primary-residence designation, their claim payments and voided payments and the NFIP policy's applied Elevation Certificates are read. The NFIP policy's applied certificates are the Elevation Certificates recorded as received on it and applied to its rating. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

## Tier figures used (identical on every tier)

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Credit threshold, lowest floor above base flood elevation | 2 whole feet |
| Elevation credit | 15 percent, so a multiplier of 0.85 where the threshold is met |
| Maximum certificate age | 10 years, that is 120 whole months from survey date to the date received |

## Input — judgement — output

| Source found | Test | Elevation multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| accepted certificate on the excess policy record | its whole-foot figure is 2 or more | 0.85 |
| accepted certificate on the excess policy record | its whole-foot figure is below 2 | 1 |
| none on the excess record; latest applied certificate of the NFIP policy of the home surveyed 120 whole months or fewer before it was received | certified lowest floor elevation less certified base flood elevation is 2 or more | 0.85 |
| as above | that difference is below 2 | 1 |
| none on the excess record; the latest applied NFIP certificate is older than that, or there is none | — | no elevation credit |

Only the certificate received latest is considered on the NFIP policy; an older applied certificate is not read in its place. Age example (hypothetical): surveyed on 1 March and received on 20 March ten years later is 120 whole months and qualifies; received on 1 April ten years later is 121 whole months and does not.
